_comment: Execution role for ALL 5 llmops worker harnesses (data-prep, finetune, eval, deploy, monitor). Extends deploy/iam/execution_role_base.json (the agentcore-harness-builder skill baseline) with the pipeline's needs: S3 run/report/skills-mirror prefixes, teacher-model Bedrock access (DeepSeek-R1), scoped SageMaker lifecycle + model registry, CloudWatch/Logs read for monitoring, and the llmops-pipeline event bus. Placeholders <REGION>, <ACCOUNT_ID>, <DATA_BUCKET>, <MEMORY_ID> are substituted by deploy/01_iam.py at deploy time (account id from sts get-caller-identity — never committed). SCOPING NOTE: the base's InvokeModel statement was foundation-model/* + inference-profile/* — here it is narrowed to exactly the models this pipeline uses (anthropic.* for the harness model global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 incl. cross-region routing targets, deepseek.r1* as the distillation teacher), so the teacher grant is NOT a duplicate statement but a narrowing of the base one. BYOMemory* statements are dropped by 01_iam.py unless --memory-id is passed (deploy/wire_memory.py re-adds them per-Memory later, matching the base's contract). Statements with Resource '*' (BaselineImagePull, BaselineTelemetry, SageMakerList, CloudWatchMetricsRead) are actions that do not support resource-level permissions.

Statement._comment: finops/* and contracts/* are the audit runtime's two paths and were both missing until a live pricing_refresh proved it: the agent derived a complete 37-SKU rate card, then failed to write it (PutObject denied on finops/rates/rate_card_latest.json) AND failed to load the canonical cost_model.py (GetObject denied on contracts/), so it published nothing and stamped its own output non-canonical. A prefix nobody granted is a feature that runs to completion and then throws its work away.

The skill trees an s3 skill source fetches at SESSION START, under THIS role -- not under the deployer's credentials. deploy/03_storage.py mirrors them to skills/<repo-relative path>/ and read-back verified each SKILL.md, but that read-back ran as the admin who deployed; simulate_principal_policy for this role on skills/llmops/llm-agent-orchestration/SKILL.md returned implicitDeny, so switching a source to s3 would have been accepted by UpdateHarness, reported READY, and then failed every single session. GetObject only, and deliberately NOT folded into S3PipelineObjects: that statement carries PutObject, and an agent that can write its own skill tree can rewrite the instructions it is judged against on the next session. S3PipelineObjects previously granted Get+Put on a skills-mirror/* prefix instead; that prefix never held a single object in the bucket's lifetime, nothing in the repo ever wrote to it, and it was writable, so it is removed here rather than reused.

The customer's own data: readable, never writable. Both prompts point data-prep at customer-data/ and nothing granted it, so the first real consult run dispatched, reached DataPrepGenerate and died on s3:ListBucket/GetObject without reading one task. Read-only because a pipeline that can rewrite the customer's data can destroy the held-out set its own gates are judged on.

The prefix list must match S3PipelineObjects: ListBucket is condition-scoped, so a prefix granted for Get/Put but absent here can be read object-by-object and never enumerated -- which is exactly the shape of 'the rate card history is there but the agent reports no card exists'. cost/* joined both lists after the first live reconcile completed its evidence-gathering and then could not write cost/actuals-<period>.json — the docs/COST.md contract names cost/ as the actuals+report prefix, but only finops/ was ever granted.

gen_ai.usage token spans land in the aws/spans log group (an AgentCore-managed group OUTSIDE /aws/bedrock-agentcore/*, so BaselineLogs does not cover it). The finops reconcile task needs to read them to attribute shared Bedrock inference-profile spend per session id — this account runs other agents on the same Claude profiles, so without spans the shared spend is unattributable and stays pending. Read-only, this one group.

For llmops_finops (the audit runtime). READ-ONLY on billing, by design: an auditor able to change what it audits is not an auditor. Every verb here is a read -- notably NO ce:CreateCostCategoryDefinition, NO ce:UpdateCostAllocationTagsStatus, NO budgets:ModifyBudget. budgets:ViewBudget is the read: the Budgets API authorizes DescribeBudgets against the IAM action budgets:ViewBudget, so a policy naming only budgets:DescribeBudgets denies the call (live AccessDeniedException named budgets:ViewBudget). Both are listed -- ViewBudget is the one enforced. Resource must be * because ce:* and pricing:* have no resource-level ARNs; the scoping is the verb list. All six harnesses share this role, so the other five gain read-only billing visibility they do not use -- the alternative is a second execution role, which the harness create path does not support today.

The finops agent reads estimates to compare against, and reads/writes the actuals ledger it owns. It must NOT be able to change an approval decision, so no write verbs on llmops-cost-estimates -- an auditor that can flip a rejected estimate to approved has defeated the gate.
